name: settings-menu-item
description:
the app menu's Settings item opens the Atrium settings window.

It needs its own route and its own test because main_menu_builder.mm wires this item with an explicit target and action on the app delegate, which bypasses commandDispatch and therefore the IDC_OPTIONS intercept entirely. Un-gating that intercept would have brought the item back for nothing.

Driven by two real clicks - the Atrium menu, then the Settings item - at coordinates read off a captured frame. The menu is the stock app menu, so its geometry is Chromium's, not ours.

The click assertion was measured ABSENT on a run that opened the menu and stopped there, so it cannot pass on the menu merely appearing.

actions.note: Atrium frontmost, so its menu bar is the one on screen
the Atrium menu in the menu bar
MEASUREMENT: the open menu, for reading the Settings item's coordinate
THE MEASUREMENT: the Settings item, at a coordinate read off the measurement run's frame. It rendered ENABLED there, which is the validateMenuItem answer this task had to decide
let the window build and its route load

assertions.label: the-item-was-retargeted-at-startup
assertions.note: the hook found the item and repointed it. Without this the click would be measuring the stock item

assertions.label: the-item-was-clicked
assertions.note: measured ABSENT on the run that only opened the menu, so it can only come from the click on the item
the browser window AND the settings window
